thread:
maria: Heads-up: launching a docs style linter + a formal SDK compatibility/deprecation policy this quarter.

jason: Nice. What problem are we aiming to solve?

maria: Reduce surprise breakages for customers and keep examples accurate. Linter will catch stale snippets, invalid example JSON, and obvious API renames. Policy defines notice windows and how we surface deprecations.

kevin: Apply to all first-party SDKs?

maria: Yes — python, js, go, rust. Third-party integrations are out of scope.

elaine: Linter mechanics?

maria: docs-lint v1 runs as a pre-merge check on docs PRs and nightly across the site. Key rules:

`````
rules:
 - snippet-lang: [python,javascript,go]
 - example-json-valid
 - no-uses-of-deprecated-fields
`````

Also supports exclude paths for archival pages.

docs-bot: nightly run scheduled; first job: 2026-05-02T02:00:00Z. Failures will auto-open issues.

tim: Policy details?

maria: Two tiers: minor param deprecations get 90 days; breaking SDK interface changes get 180 days. We'll add banner notices in docs, changelog entries in releases, and targeted comms for enterprise customers.

sara: New labels / workflow?

maria: Use `docs/deprecation`, `docs/lint-fix`, and `sdk/compat` on GH. We'll also publish a /docs/migrations/<release> folder with migration snippets.

jason: Rollout timeline?

maria: Beta linter opt-in May 2, enforced May 16. Policy effective immediately for new deprecation announcements.

elaine: I'll prepare the docs-ops checklist and a short runbook for triage.

maria: Thanks — I'll post the draft linter config at https://git.redwood.ai/docs-lint/draft and will assign initial triage issues to docs-ops.

jason: :thumbsup: 

docs-bot: created issue #3421: docs-lint flagged 7 warnings in docs/getting-started

kevin: Thanks — will follow up on the SDK side.
